newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia Suharto says many want to see him ill.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia Suharto says many want to see him ill.

text.p: Indonesian President Suharto said on Friday that many people hoped he would fall ill but the prayers of the Indonesian people were keeping him healthy.
Speaking to schoolchildren who visited the State Palace in Jakarta, the 75-year-old president thanked them for their prayers for his good health and long life.

"Thank you for your prayers and maybe God will answer them. If they are answered I will be happy. It is better than I am healthy rather than sick although many are praying in order that I become sick," Suharto said.
"Overseas the news is that I am sick. In fact it is not so. Why is that? Because of the prayers of the people of Indonesia, including yours. Thank you," he said.
Last month financial markets rocked on rumours that Suharto, who has ruled Indonesia for more than 30 years, was unwell.
Suharto, who has no designated sucessor, visited a German heart clinic for tests last July and was declared in good health for a man of his age.
Indonesia's Peoples Consultative Assembly (MPR) will elect the next president next March and Suharto is widely expected to run for his seventh term.
His nomination has never been opposed by the body, in which he appoints a majority of members.
In an unusual move, Suharto's half-brother Probosutedjo on Thursday denied rumours that the president had remarried or planned to do so.
"It is completely slanderous and totally untrue," Probosutedjo was quoted as saying by the Antara news agency.

Jakarta has been thick with rumours for weeks that Suharto was waiting for the marriage of his youngest son, Hutomo Mandala Putra, to remarry. Mandala Putra was married to a descendant of Javanese royalty on Wednesday.
Suharto's wife of 48 years, Tien, died of a heart attack in April 1996.
Probosutedjo said he had checked with Suharto and was told by the president that the rumours were untrue.
